text.p: French glassmaker Saint-Gobain SA said on Thursday its 1996 net attributable profit would be 4.32 billion francs, up slightly from 4.21 billion last year.

The company said the provisional result proved "the solidity of the group in a poor European economic environment, especially in the building sector, that is compensated by sustained activity on the American continent."
It said the profit was booked after 1.2 billion in restructuring charges.

Chairman Jean-Louis Beffa said in a telephone interview that the 1997 result would show good progress due to the asset gain on the sale of a majority stake in contract management firm Cise to a subsidiary of building company Bouygues for 2.16 billion francs.
He declined to give a prediction for pre-exceptional results, saying it was too early to do so.
Beffa said the restructuring charges, more than double the 569 million francs of provisions set aside in 1995, showed the company's willingness to tackle its problems.
"The profit figure is in line with what the market expected -- but after charges which were higher than expected," Beffa told Reuters.
"The charges -- of 1.2 billion -- are very high and show our willingness to improve our European cost structure," he said.
Sales rose to 91.35 billion francs from 70.31 billion, due largely to the acquisition of building materials company Poliet. On a comparable basis, Saint-Gobain's sales were up 2.1 percent.
